purpose: Query console HTTP server entrypoint with request validation, routing, and source snippet retrieval

mechanics.responsibility: Maintain the canonical mapping of pathname → allowed HTTP methods

semantic.purpose: Fallback map when routing contract is unavailable or rejected
semantic.completeness: AUTHORITATIVE — this is the canonical list. No routes should be added without legal review of security implications.

decisions.why: This map is residual, mechanical-only. It exists solely to choose 404 vs 405 when the authority (route-dispatch.authority.json) rejects a request. It is NOT the routing decision itself — that authority is external.
decisions.omitted_routes: Routes NOT in this list receive 404. This is intentional — unknown routes are rejected.
decisions.field_completeness: All routes defined in route-dispatch.authority.json MUST be in this map, or 404 becomes ambiguous.
decisions.why_not_auto_generated: This map is MANUALLY MAINTAINED because routing authority is externally sourced. Any mismatch between this map and route-dispatch.authority.json is a bug.

mechanics.responsibility: Ensure query console server binds ONLY to loopback (127.0.0.1)

semantic.guard_purpose: Only catch and transform THIS specific error. All other errors propagate.
semantic.transformation: Re-throw with clearer message: 'The query console server may bind only to 127.0.0.1.'
semantic.errorMessage: The query console server may bind only to 127.0.0.1.
semantic.why_loopback_only: Query console is an internal development tool. It MUST NOT be exposed to network interfaces. Binding to 0.0.0.0, ::, or any external IP is a security violation.

decisions.is_canonical: YES — this is canonical failure behavior, not error recovery
decisions.error_message_clarity: The message clearly states the constraint (loopback only) and the remedy
decisions.why_not_auto_recoverable: There is no fallback for this constraint. Loopback binding is non-negotiable.

mechanics.notes: Lines 42-47 are a decision point (line 45 branch) + exception handling (line 42 catch)

mechanics.responsibility: Validate that index is provided and is a loaded source-fact-index.v1 object

semantic.why_required: The entire server depends on an index to answer queries. No index = no functionality.

decisions.why_null_check: Caller might not provide index, or might provide null. Both are errors.
decisions.why_typeof_check: Caller might provide a scalar or string instead of an object
decisions.recovery_allowed: NO — this is a hard requirement
decisions.blame_assignment: Caller's responsibility to provide a valid index

mechanics.responsibility: Validate that consoleAssetPath is provided and is a non-empty string

semantic.why_required: The server must serve the console UI HTML from a file path. Missing or empty path = no UI.

decisions.why_trim_check: Allow whitespace-only strings to be treated as empty (invalid)
decisions.recovery_allowed: NO — this is a hard requirement
decisions.blame_assignment: Caller's responsibility to provide a valid asset path

mechanics.responsibility: Ensure security headers are always sent, even after errors

semantic.precondition: response exists and is an HTTP response object
semantic.effect: Security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) are written to response
semantic.why_guard: Cannot write headers twice. If an error occurred and headers were already sent, this invocation is skipped.
semantic.why_always_needed: Every response MUST include security headers, regardless of success or error path

decisions.is_idempotent: NO — headers can only be written once
decisions.why_not_redundant: The guard ensures headers are written exactly once, not multiple times
decisions.what_if_error_first: If handlesRequest throws and headers already sent, this is skipped. That means some responses might have incomplete headers. This is acceptable because the error was already sent.
decisions.precondition_safety: The precondition (response object existence) is guaranteed by the HTTP server

mechanics.responsibility: Serialize error responses as JSON with error message field

semantic.why_json: Console expects application/json responses. Even errors must be JSON.

decisions.error_shape: AUTHORITATIVE — errors are { error: 'message' }. No stack traces, no error codes, just message.
decisions.why_simple: Console UI knows how to parse and display { error: ... } responses
decisions.why_no_code: Error codes are internal. Console just shows the message.
decisions.why_no_stack: Stack traces are server secrets and must not be exposed

mechanics.responsibility: Route errors by disposition: re-throw external errors, handle HOSTNAME_NOT_ADMITTED

semantic.false_branch: continue to line 46 (throw new Error with message)

decisions.why_check_disposition: The callee (classifiesLoopbackBind) signals errors via disposition field. Only HOSTNAME_NOT_ADMITTED should be caught here.
decisions.why_re_throw: All other errors are unexpected. They indicate bugs in classifiesLoopbackBind or its callees.
decisions.why_not_catch_all: If we caught all errors, we'd mask unexpected exceptions
decisions.ordering: Check disposition first. If not the expected error, fail immediately.
decisions.completeness: This is the ONLY place in the file where we check error?.disposition

mechanics.responsibility: Build line array with context from firstLine to lastLine, marking hit lines

body: Determine hit flag: lineNumber >= startLine && lineNumber <= endLine
Push object { line: lineNumber, text, hit } to lines array
semantic.why_lineNumber_minus_1: Array is 0-indexed, line numbers are 1-indexed. Convert to access allLines.

decisions.is_order_significant: YES — lines must be returned in ascending order
decisions.what_if_empty: If firstLine > lastLine, loop doesn't execute and lines = []
decisions.why_hit_flag: Consumer (console UI) highlights which lines are the actual 'snippet' (startLine-endLine) vs context
decisions.why_text_from_array: allLines was pre-split from file content. Access by index is direct and O(1).
decisions.why_this_order: Frontend expects lines in order so they render correctly in the UI

mechanics.responsibility: Normalize path segments by splitting on both forward and back slashes

semantic.canonicalForm: Array of segments split by / and \
semantic.why_both_slashes: Windows paths use \ but users might provide /, so normalize to canonical array

mechanics.responsibility: Normalize line endings (CRLF, CR) to LF before splitting

semantic.canonicalForm: Array of lines split on \n after normalization
semantic.why_needed: Files from different platforms use different line endings. Normalize to \n for consistency

mechanics.responsibility: Platform-aware path case normalization for comparison

semantic.canonicalForm: Normalized path for comparison (lowercase on Windows, original on Unix)
semantic.why_needed: Windows paths are case-insensitive, Unix are case-sensitive. Normalize for safe comparison
